title: Symmetric Locality: Definition and Initial Results
problem: Data movement is a bottleneck in high-performance computation. The paper characterizes symmetric locality through repeated traversals based on symmetric group theory to improve cache and memory performance.
motivation: Understanding and optimizing symmetric locality patterns can reduce memory movement overhead in high-performance algorithms and systems.
method: The work studies repeated traversals (re-traversals) based on symmetric group theory to characterize symmetric locality. It generalizes previously known results like cyclic and sawtooth traces to arbitrary re-traversals. An abstract framework is provided for compiler design and machine learning applications to optimize memory performance.
key_novelty: Generalization of re-traversal patterns based on symmetric group theory to characterize and optimize memory performance.
contributions: Characterization framework for symmetric locality through repeated traversals
Generalization of cyclic and sawtooth traces to any re-traversal pattern
Abstract framework applicable to compiler design and machine learning optimization
limitations: Specific experimental validation, performance metrics, and practical applications are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Theoretical characterization of symmetric locality for memory optimization
